title: Automatic turn-to-memory capture replaces explicit reporting
context: Previously, tasks only entered the memory system when an agent explicitly reported them, creating gaps in the record of work. This left undefined what happened during turns without explicit agent reports, and required manual session grouping for continuity.
decision: All turns automatically create memory records, regardless of agent reporting. Follow-up prompts within a session are grouped into a single episode record anchored to the git changes they produce. Verification timeouts prevent dead runners from blocking task completion.
consequences: Complete coverage of developer activity—no lost turns
Implicit session coherence: related prompts auto-group into episodes
Memory records grounded in concrete git diffs (empirical anchoring)
Larger corpus of task records (higher signal density, potential noise)
Reduced deadlocking when verification infrastructure fails
alternatives_rejected: Keep opt-in reporting: loses turns without explicit agent summaries
Report every action separately: fragments related work across records
Manual episode grouping: requires user overhead
